endorsements.quote: This includes clear documentation of data preprocessing steps, sample size justifications, modelling decisions, hyperparameter tuning strategies (eg, grid or random search), feature selection techniques (including filter methods like correlation analysis, wrapper methods like recursive feature elimination, or embedded methods such as least absolute shrinkage and selection operator [LASSO]), model performance evaluation methods and metrics, and model explanation methods (eg, Shapley Additive Explanations [SHAP] [ 12 ], Submodular Pick Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations [SP-LIME] [ 13 ], and Counterfactual Explanations for Robustness, Transparency, Interpretability, and Fairness of Artificial Intelligence [CERTIFAI] models [ 14 ]).
This highlights the need for comprehensive evaluation across multiple performance domains, including discrimination, calibration, classification metrics, clinical utility, and fairness.

Moreover, LR’s well-recognized interpretability and trustworthiness [ 24 ] further reinforce its widespread use in clinical prediction modelling, and it is typically used as a reference model for performance benchmarking in ML studies.

unlisted_practices: Choose the modelling algorithm according to the structure, quality, and characteristics of the dataset.
Adhere to minimum sample size recommendations when developing clinical prediction models to improve stability of predictions.
Assess the stability of model predictions, not only differences in performance, when comparing modelling approaches.
Policymakers and funding bodies should prioritize investment in data quality infrastructure, including standardized phenotyping, consistent variable definitions, and robust data curation practices.
Reorient clinical prediction modelling from a model-centric to a data-centric paradigm.
Apply thoughtful data preprocessing when developing clinical prediction models.
Discuss relevant features and desired trade-offs with stakeholders such as health care providers and patients to guide model development.
Expand the candidate predictors available in health data, for example by integrating lifestyle factors collected through wearables and medical devices.
Use clinical prediction models as a second set of eyes complementing clinical judgment rather than replacing it.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary synthesizing comparative studies and arguing for a shift toward data quality over model complexity in clinical prediction modeling.
